newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypobank direct unit still in the red - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Hypobank direct unit still in the red - magazine.

text.p: Direkt Anlage Bank (DAB), the direct banking arm of Germany's Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank AG, is still in the red in its third year of operation, unit manager Ralf Miller said this weekend.
In an interview with German magazine "Bank Magazin", Miller said the dicount brokerage had just 21,300 active clients, but needed 30,000 to 35,000 to turn a profit.
At the same time, Miller said, "DAB will be the first direct bank (in Germany) to make a profit for its parent."

Miller said that DAB, unlike the other German direct banks which have cropped up in recent years, had the advantage of focusing on low-cost and low-maintenance securities transactions rather than labour-intensive current accounts.
In 1996, a boom year for the German stock exchange, DAB averaged 12 transactions per customer, 50 percent more than the previous year and above its goal of 12 transactions per customer per year.
